QF.id: AIFM CIII Governance and Due Diligence_3

question.text: Ms. Priya Shah, CIO of Aravalli Long-Short Fund (Cat III AIF), is conducting Investor Due Diligence on a proposed investee company. Which of the following is typically delivered by the investee's team into a 'virtual data room' for IDD review?

answer.text: Investment manager's in-house Conflict of Interest Register
SEBI's Compliance Test Report for the AIF
Constitutional documents (MoA/AoA), board minutes, books of account, tax returns, and audited financials

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the chapter, 'data room' records for IDD typically include constitutional documents (MoA/AoA), board minutes and reports, books of account, tax returns, invoices, purchase orders, payroll, statutory filings, property agreements, IP documentation, employee lists, segment financials and historical audited financials — these flow from INVESTEE to the AIF manager's investment team. The Trap: The other three options are AIF-side internal documents, not investee-company IDD deliverables. They test whether the candidate confuses AIF-internal records with the investee-company data room. Cross-Exam Context: Same data-room concept appears in XIX-C/D but framed for Cat I/II PE due diligence; XIX-E frames it from the Cat III hedge fund manager desk (even block-trade private placements on listed-name special situations require similar IDD rigour). Manager's Pro-Tip: For Cat III event-driven or activist plays on listed names, run a lightweight IDD on the TRIGGER event (M&A, spin-off, buy-back) — focus the virtual data room on deal-specific docs (scheme, valuation report, auditor qualifications) rather than full-PE vintage paperwork.
